did.head: Descriptive Summary
did.unittitle: State Park Drawings and Plans of the Virginia Dept. of Conservation and Recreation [DRAFT], 1933-1941

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: State Park Drawings and Plans of the Virginia Dept. of Conservation and Recreation, 1930-1950. Accession 54943, State government records collection, The Library of Virginia, Richmond, Va.

bioghist.head: Historical Information
bioghist.p: In 1926 the Virginia General Assembly passed at act creating the Virginia State Commission on Conservation and Development as a single agency responsible for managing the conservation of its natural resources. In 1930, as interest in establishing a state park system grew, the Commission conducted a study of the development, operation, maintenance and administration of state parks in other states. This study became the basis for the development and management of Virginia's State Park System. In 1933 the General Assembly allocated $50,000 in funds for parkland acquisition and it took the Commonwealth less than a year to acquire, both by gift and purchase, large tracts of land for establishment of the initial parks. The establishment of the federal Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) by President Roosevelt in 1933 provided the means and manpower for the development of the parks. On June 15, 1936, the first six state parks were opened simultaneously, including Douthat State Park, Fairy Stone State Park, Hungry Mother State Park, Seashore State Park, Staunton River State Park, and Westmoreland State Park.

Master plans were developed for each park and Civilian Conservation Corps camps were established at each location. Between 1933-1942, the men employed at these camps built recreational facilities and amenities for swimming, hiking, fishing and camping. They cleared trails, built roads, dams and spillways, erected cabins and other structures, established swimming beaches and picnic areas, and other amenites for visitors. The design approach for the parks relied heavily on the integration of structures with the natural environment and the use of local materials.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Virginia State Parks drawings and plans, 1933-1941, include plans, architectural and schematic drawings, and topography maps. Plans include park master plans, as well as plans for planting, trails, dams and spilways, trailer and tent campgrounds, electric lines, water lines (water treatment facilities) and roads, including bridges, culverts, retention walls, and guardrails. Includes architectural drawings for recreational facilities including cabins, cottages, dwellings for the park custodian and superintendent, bath houses, boat docks, picnic shelters, latrines, bunkhouses, restaurants, information centers, and lodges, as well as for maintenance buildings, such as tool shops, blacksmith shops, oil and paint shops, garages, and administrative buildings. Also includes detail schematics for original iron work fixtures for hinges, latches, lighting and door handles and knobs; furniture, window fixtures, fountains, boat docks, campstoves.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This collection is arranged in original order.

did.unittitle: Douthat State Park, 1930-1950.

scopecontent.p: Douthat State Park is located in the Alleghany Mountains of western Virginia, spanning across Alleghaney County and Bath County. A consortium of Virginia business formed the Douthat Land Company to purchase land and donated the initial 1,920 acres of the present park, with the state purchasing the remainder of the property. The park encompasses 4,545 acres and includes 50-acre lake.
